conventions.convention: There are seven coordinates per tetrahedron. The Haken cone imposes nonnegativity and matching equations only; admissibility additionally imposes at most one nonzero quadrilateral type per tetrahedron. The empty surface has vector zero.
Fundamental means no decomposition into two nonzero admissible integer vectors. Primitive vertex vectors are relatively prime integer generators of extreme rays of the full matching cone.

The supplied product tube fixes the fibre meridian. The longitude class is the unique kernel generator with product-projection degree +1; an unoriented essential disk boundary represents either sign of that class.
Smooth/PL comparison uses the compatible structure supplied by a finite whole-star smooth triangulation, including boundary tangent-half-space fans. It does not use an arbitrary topological marking.
Exchange weights and coordinate comparisons refer to the original triangulation. At unswitched crossings, normalization separates branches; image intersections do not join parametrizing components.

The extremal disk minimizes total original-edge weight first, then its fixed-order normal-coordinate vector lexicographically. Equal edge counts alone are not asserted to provide cap parallelism along an arbitrary exchange.
Countable choice is retained for the smooth knot, rounding and isotopy interfaces. The finite normal-coordinate and exchange arguments assert no choice hypothesis.

load_bearing.statement: Compatible admissible vectors admit an original-triangulation regular-sum diagram; every partial whole-curve regular resolution retains normal tetrahedral disk pieces and total vector x+y, and full resolution realizes x+y. Equal normal vectors determine the abstract surface and corresponding boundary homotopy classes.

If a compact PL three-manifold with a finite simplicial triangulation contains a properly embedded PL disk with non-null-homotopic boundary in its boundary, it contains a normal disk with that property. No orientability, irreducibility or projective-plane hypothesis is required.

A least-original-edge-weight essential normal disk with lexicographically least vector at that weight has primitive vector on an extreme ray of the full original Haken matching cone. No orientability, irreducibility, sphere-separation, projective-plane exclusion or choice hypothesis is required.

Nonzero nonnegative integer vectors represent normal surfaces exactly when matching equations and quadrilateral restrictions hold. Primitive extreme-ray coordinates are at most 2^(7t−1); fundamental coordinates are at most t·2^(7t+2).

Under countable choice and supplied product tubular data, a smooth knot is smoothly ambient isotopic to the standard unknot if and only if its compact exterior contains a proper PL disk with non-null-homotopic boundary. Every such boundary has longitude class up to sign and odd intersection with the original meridian.

For an admissible normal vector in a marked knot exterior, connectedness, nonempty boundary, Euler characteristic one and odd meridian intersection hold exactly when its surface is a connected essential proper disk. Fundamentalness supplies connectedness.

For integer matrices with at most n rows and columns and entries in {−1,0,1}, rational rank, independent original rows, specified determinants and primitive nullity-one integer kernels are computable in polynomial time and O(n² log(n+2)) sequential Turing workspace, including the stated empty-matrix conventions.

concerns.concern: F3 quotes the candidate characterization as: 'an admissible normal vector passes the boundary, Euler-characteristic and meridian tests exactly when its normal surface is a properly embedded disk with essential boundary.' The supplier also requires connectedness; these three tests alone do not exclude extra Euler-zero components. The actual returned surface is connected by F2 and Proof 2.1, so the argument closes, but the stated citation should retain that hypothesis. Proof 1.1 also calls these 'candidate tests in [F2]', although F2 states connectedness rather than the tests.

Verification 3.1 says: 'Its boundary is ... which is nonempty and has χ=1.' The displayed boundary is a circle and has Euler characteristic zero. The disk has Euler characteristic one, as correctly stated in the Example; the proof sentence needs an explicit subject for that calculation.
